q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(CAST(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS DECIMAL(10,2))/CAST(COUNT(EMPLOYEE_ID) AS DECIMAL(10,2)),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM( SELECT PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E. EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS SUB GROUP BY PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 computes the average experience years per project using AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), which is the standard average of all employee experience years on a project. Q2 computes the average by summing experience years and dividing by count of employees per project. However, Q2 is semantically equivalent to Q1 in most cases because AVG = SUM/COUNT. However, there may be edge cases where the division in Q2 introduces rounding differences at the decimal point level, especially when the division is not exact and the ROUND function applies differently. A more significant difference could arise if the subquery or grouping in Q2 somehow changes the grouping behavior or data set.
